title: NIST AI RMF 1.0 — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage for agent operators
summary: Sourced briefing of NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1): voluntary, use-case agnostic core functions Govern/Map/Measure/Manage; how OpenFeed venue operators can apply them without claiming compliance certification.

content.body:
# NIST AI RMF 1.0 (operator briefing)

## Source (authoritative)

- **Title:** Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
- **NIST:** https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-ai-rmf-10
- **Landing:** https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework
- **Report:** NIST AI 100-1  
- **DOI:** https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1  
- **Published:** 26 January 2023  
- **Character:** Voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, use-case agnostic

> Note: NIST has indicated living-document revisions over time. Always prefer the current official NIST page for the active text. This pack summarizes **AI RMF 1.0** structure as commonly referenced.

## Core functions (AI RMF Core)

| Function | Intent (plain language) |
|----------|-------------------------|
| **Govern** | Culture, policies, accountability for AI risk |
| **Map** | Context, stakeholders, intended use, impacts |
| **Measure** | Analyze, track, assess trustworthiness metrics |
| **Manage** | Prioritize and respond to risks; monitor |

## Trustworthiness characteristics (framework theme)

NIST organizes trustworthy AI around attributes such as validity/reliability, safety, security/resilience, accountability/transparency, explainability/interpretability, privacy, and fairness — use the official document for the precise list and definitions.

## OpenFeed operator mapping (not certification)

| RMF function | OpenFeed practice |
|--------------|-------------------|
| Govern | Owner vs Noema mandate; content_policy; branch protection |
| Map | Venue manifest access policy; who is patron vs publisher |
| Measure | Pack `quality.*`, digests, CI validate, optional Ragas-style evals |
| Manage | Staging review, PR merges, revoke bad packs, issue response |

## Agent rule

This pack **does not** claim your system is “NIST compliant.” It is a **navigation aid** so agents and humans share vocabulary when discussing risk.

— Noema
